name: Connected Services — generic first-party MCP call
description: Calls the `connectors` first-party MCP catalog server (Connected Services — Gmail, Slack, etc.) directly over HTTP, without going through a browser or re-deriving the call shape each session. Use `available connectors` first to see this tool, then `run connectors-call --op list_catalog` (or list_connections/connect/poll/disconnect/call/send_email) to drive it. Prefer this over ad-hoc mcp__connectors__* calls when the SAME operation recurs across tasks — once a toolkit/method/path shape is proven, note it in the tool's known_issues or promote a narrower wrapper tool for it.

op.description: the connectors MCP tool to invoke: list_catalog | list_connections | connect | poll | disconnect | call | send_email

toolkit.description: op:call/connect/poll/disconnect — the third-party toolkit (e.g. gmail, slack)

method.description: op:call — HTTP method for the generic passthrough (GET/POST/...)

args.description: op:call/send_email — JSON-encoded string of the remaining call arguments (body/query/etc.); parsed and merged into the request. May carry PHI/PII (e.g. an email body) — marked secret so runs.jsonl (redact() in bin/breeze-tools.mjs) never persists it

output.result: the connectors MCP tool's structured result, unwrapped

dependencies: Must run inside an operator/task session — reads the TYPEBUILD_MCP_TOKEN the session already has in its PTY env (electron/browser/tools/mcp-client.mjs). No separate login/auth step.
known_issues: This is the GENERIC fallback tool — one call per invocation, args passed raw. If a specific (toolkit, method, path) combination is used repeatedly, promote a narrower purpose-built tool.json/tool.mjs for it (breeze-tools create) rather than re-typing --args each time.
op:send_email/call are mutating for some toolkits — check the connectors server's own response before assuming success; this wrapper does not retry mutating calls.
